explanation: Fires on the current token when it is a person noun that is specifically female through kinship, marriage or title (aunt, niece, wife, mother, mom, daughter, widow, princess, bride, grandmother, queen, nun, actress, sister, girlfriend: about 0.3-0.75 of max, with or without a possessive), and much more weakly on their male counterparts (husband, son, father, dad, groom, boyfriend, actor, prince: about 0.1-0.25; uncle and nephew are exceptions at about 0.4-0.5). Generic or non-relational person words (woman, girl, lady, man, she, Mary, lawyer, landlord) and abstract or expository text stay near zero. Concrete everyday nouns and verbs (car, boat, drove, cattle) give a weak background of up to about 0.35 of max. A narrow separate case is the first piece of a few famous split names (' Odys' in Odyssey, ' Boh' in Bohr, ' Heisenberg': about 0.6-0.9).
